subject.title: fix: keep exec approval carriers scoped [AI]

question: Should persistent exec allow-always policy treat POSIX `command`, `builtin`, and `exec` as transparent carriers and bind approval to the carried executable?
rationale: This is an authorization-policy contract: tests and proof show the intended behavior, but they cannot decide the product/security semantics for existing persisted approvals.

options.title: Approve scoped carrier unwrapping
options.body: Accept the POSIX-only transparent-carrier contract, including fail-closed handling for ambiguous forms and `command -p`.

options.title: Keep carriers as approval identities
options.body: Reject this policy change and retain the existing behavior that evaluates carrier invocations without unwrapping them.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped carrier unwrapping
recommendation.body: Accept the POSIX-only transparent-carrier contract, including fail-closed handling for ambiguous forms and `command -p`.

likelyOwner.reason: Likely repository-level decision owner for the core exec-approval security boundary; exact file-history ownership could not be established from the read-only environment.
